newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin offers liberal job as first deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin offers liberal job as first deputy PM.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin offered on Monday the post of first deputy prime minister to the liberal governor of the Nizhny Novgorod region, Boris Nemtsov, Russian news agencies said.
Yeltsin had previously said there would be only one person with this title in the new Russian government -- reformer Anatoly Chubais.
Itar-Tass news agency reported the invitation to Nemtsov, 37, and Interfax news agency said he had accepted.

Interfax quoted sources as saying Nemtsov would be in charge of natural monopolies, the social sphere and relations with regional authorities. There was no immediate confirmation of the report from the Kremlin.

"There is a very interesting variant," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as telling Nemtsov. "Two young men -- you and Anatoly Chubais -- create a fresh young team in the government -- from scratch. No one (else) has been appointed yet. All candidates to the government will be agreed with the two first deputy premiers."
Yeltsin was due to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Chubais later on Tuesday to discuss the government reshuffle ordered by the Kremlin leader. REUTER
